text:
Ms. Albright used to have a uniform, navy blue polyester that wouldn't hang right, would just stick out from your body. Really awful material. She hated that uniform. Used to get a rash around the collar because it was so stiff and starched. She's here in her classroom now, thirty years later. And this uniform is nicer, it's a softer cotton, it fits better, it's more comfortable. But it does the same thing. That sea of navy and white. It kind of erases a lot of who they are.
There's a boy in the back row who's new, Leo. And his uniform is too big, his blazer, the sleeves, he just has his hands in there. And he keeps pulling on the collar, tugging on the button. He's making this little cathedral out of paperclips. He's got it on his desk, in silent reading. Everyone's reading. He's just making this little cathedral or spaceship out of paperclips. She walks over. He looks up at her. He looks at her with this big eyes, like, uh oh. And she just kneels down. She says, "That is beautiful. What is it?" He just shrugs and says, "Just a thing." And she says, "It looks like a place where I would want to live. A place with no rules." And he smiles just a little bit. He looks at her suit, her grey suit, her very sensible shoes. He looks at the uniformity of her. And then he looks away.
Then at recess she watches him. He's over by the fence and he's not with the other kids. He's just drawing in the dirt with his toe. And they're all playing kickball. He's just drawing in the dirt. And the uniform makes him look very separate from them. It doesn't really include him, it just separates him from the rest of them. And it's a very sad thing. He's just looking very lost.
And then he leaves and she has a note on her desk that a little girl has written. A very shy girl. Chloe. Who hardly talks. And it says, "Leo's paperclip thing was cool." And she looks over at Chloe. Chloe is very neat. Her uniform is very neat, no wrinkles. She's very neat. And she's packing her bag and very quietly. But she looked at Leo's paperclip cathedral and thought it was cool. And she saw him.
And then they leave. And Ms. Albright stays in the classroom. And the room is very quiet. And she thinks about how she hated the uniform. And how it erases people. And it's her job to find who they are underneath the uniform. She walks over to the back and Leo left his little paperclip cathedral there. And he left it very carefully. And next to it he has a little button. A button from the uniform. He put it there very carefully, very deliberately. And Ms. Albright picks up the button. It's very smooth and it's very cool and it's white. And it's just a little uniform button. And she picks it up. And it's nothing. And it's so little. But it feels very special to her. And she holds it in her fist, in her hand.
